name: The Majestic Oak

location.address: Majestic Oaks Circle (public cul-de-sac), Savannah, GA 31406

access: Free; stands alone in the centre of a public residential cul-de-sac, viewable from the public street at any time. Not on private land: the tree sits in the circle itself, with houses facing it (the listing at 2 Majestic Oaks Circle describes itself as "across from the Majestic Oak").
transport: Residential street in the Isle of Hope area of Savannah, car recommended; no transit stop nearby
verify_notes: Two independent sources: a 2013 photo-blog post (1000wordsdotkodakdotcom.wordpress.com) that says a plaque beside the tree gives its title and estimated age, quoting a base girth of 27 feet 8 inches (843 cm) and a branch span over 165 feet, calling it '300-plus-year-old'; and travelyesplease.com (2015/2025), which independently gives 300-400 years and calls it 'likely Savannah's oldest, maybe even largest tree'. A widely repeated but UNVERIFIED claim (found only in WebSearch AI summaries, never seen on a fetched page) says the tree witnessed the 1910-1911 Savannah Grand Prize auto races and was 'fully grown when Oglethorpe founded Savannah' (1733) -- dropped per the search-summary-is-a-lead-never-a-source rule; a Compass real-estate listing for the house across the street does repeat the Oglethorpe line but that is marketing copy, not a source, so it is not used as evidence, only as a location confirmation. Girth of 843cm (27'8") for a live oak is enormous, larger than many registered champion live oaks, so treat the plaque figure as the strongest evidence for remarkableness even though the exact age must stay a broad estimate. The tree is entirely separate from Wormsloe Historic Site (several km away); a popular local legend links it to the old Wormsloe Plantation but no source confirms this, so the story should not repeat it as fact. Not the Wormsloe Oak Avenue already published as sav_002.  Coordinate is geocoded to the street/circle (Roadtrippers), not from a mapped photo of the trunk, hence approximate.
